overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: candidate names need not be listed where no individual candidates were discussed, the reduced-font bulletin board notice was still legible, and the web copies differed only by the clerk's spacing change.

allegations.summary: Notice for the June 6 meeting did not list the candidates for subcommittee appointments under the 'Vote to approve' topics.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee did not discuss individual candidates, it was unnecessary to list the names of the individual appointees in this instance.

allegations.summary: The notice posted on the Town Hall bulletin board was allegedly difficult to read because the font was too small after the clerk reduced it to one page.
allegations.key_passage: While the font size of the notice was reduced by the clerk, we find that the posted notice was still printed in a legible, easily understandable format.

allegations.summary: The courtesy copies of the notice on the school and Town websites allegedly differed from each other.
allegations.key_passage: When assessing notices for compliance with the Open Meeting Law, our office looks at the notice that is posted at the official notice posting location which, in this case, is the bulletin board at Town Hall.
